question: Ventriculo-peritoneal (VP) shunt placement is the most commonly used surgical treatment for hydrocephalus in children.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. VP shunt (ventriculo-peritoneal shunt) is the most frequently performed surgical procedure for childhood hydrocephalus. It routes excess CSF from the cerebral ventricles to the peritoneal cavity via a one-way pressure-regulating valve. Medical management with acetazolamide or furosemide is only a temporising measure. Endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) is used in selected obstructive cases.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. VP shunt is the standard definitive surgical treatment for most forms of hydrocephalus in children. A catheter drains CSF from the lateral ventricle to the peritoneal cavity via a valve mechanism that regulates CSF pressure. Complications include shunt blockage, infection, over-drainage, and siphoning. Endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) is an alternative for obstructive hydrocephalus in older children.
